name: Magic Internet Money

obituary.epitaph: The magic ran out at nine cents
obituary.obituary: Once one of DeFi's largest CDP stablecoins, MIM peaked above $3.6B before repeated cauldron exploits and years of thinning liquidity hollowed out its market. The final break began on June 8, 2026. Abracadabra injected liquidity, offered SPELL incentives, raised rates across every cauldron, and suspended Curve bribes to force debt repayment, but none restored the peg. By July 26 MIM traded near $0.09 with roughly $3M circulating after seven weeks below peg, leaving no credible liquidity or arbitrage path back to one dollar.

oneLiner: MIM is Abracadabra's CDP-style stablecoin minted against interest-bearing tokens and crypto collateral in cauldron vaults, with automatic liquidations.
collateral: Interest-bearing tokens and crypto collateral deposited into active Abracadabra cauldrons, currently concentrated in yvDAI and WBTC with smaller yvWETH/WETH positions
pegMechanism: CDP-style cauldrons with overcollateralization and automatic liquidations (4% liquidation fee); borrowers are incentivized to buy MIM below $1 to repay debt; 0.5% borrow/interest fees accrue to sSPELL stakers and governance treasury

oracleRisk.summary: Abracadabra's four currently debt-bearing Ethereum cauldrons each use a single-source oracle behind an owner-swappable ProxyOracle with no timelock; three price collateral off a single Chainlink feed and the largest (yvDAI, 45.7% of tracked collateral) has no external price feed at all, valuing DAI at a hardcoded $1.

branchApplicability.reviewer: Claude Safety Score V9 curation lane (branch-level oracle/liquidation resolution)
branchApplicability.rationale: On-chain reads at Ethereum block 25579951 confirm the four cauldrons already tracked in this file's liveReservesConfig (yvWETH 0xed510639…, WETH 0x390Db10e…, WBTC 0x5ec47EE6…, yvDAI 0x7Ce7D9ED…) are the complete current debt-bearing inventory, and each has a distinct oracle, COLLATERIZATION_RATE, LIQUIDATION_MULTIPLIER, and BORROW_OPENING_FEE, so market-specific branch treatment is required rather than a single asset-level tier. Abracadabra's dev docs confirm the general mechanism ("we sometimes use Proxy Oracles, that point to a 'real' Oracle. The oracle the proxy points to can be changed by the Owner") but do not describe a system-level bad-debt or shutdown process; that residual gap is recorded per-branch below rather than left as a blanket unresolved rating.

branches.label: yvWETH collateral (Cauldron 0xed510639E1b07c9145CD570F8Dd0CA885F760E09)

branches.fallbackBehavior: No secondary feed. The ProxyOracle's oracleImplementation can be replaced by its owner (a 3-of-6 Gnosis Safe, 0xDF2C270f610Dc35d8fFDA5B453E74db5471E126B, owners confirmed via getOwners()/getThreshold() at block 25579951) with no on-chain timelock.

branches.backstop: No contractual insurance or recapitalization backstop is documented; residual cauldron bad debt has instead been addressed through ad hoc DAO treasury MIM buybacks.
branches.shutdownOrBadDebtBehavior: Abracadabra's public documentation does not describe a formal shutdown, insurance fund, or bad-debt-socialization mechanism for cauldrons; the CauldronOwner can deprecate a cauldron and cut its MIM borrow capacity, but historical under-collateralized bad debt from cauldron exploits (2024-01, 2025-03, 2025-10, recorded in this asset's mintIncidents) has been absorbed through ad hoc DAO treasury MIM buybacks rather than a documented protocol backstop.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: The verified MIM token source exposes owner-controlled mint functions and the owner is a 5-of-11 Safe. The reviewed cauldron and reserve metadata also include stablecoin collateral such as DAI, so upstream issuer freeze exposure is retained. The sources do not establish one direct holder-freeze implementation across MIM's material deployments, so no direct blacklist boolean is asserted.

mintAuthority.summary: The Ethereum MIM contract exposes owner-controlled mint functions. Owner is a 5/11 Safe with no modules or guard detected.

mintIncidents.summary: Abracadabra cauldron borrow logic was exploited to enable unauthorized MIM borrowing, turning the stablecoin mint/borrow route into bad debt.

Flawed collateral accounting in Abracadabra's GMX-integrated gmCauldrons left phantom collateral after failed deposit orders and self-liquidation, letting the attacker borrow about 13.4M MIM (~$13M in ETH) against collateral the system failed to remove.

A cook() action-sequencing flaw in deprecated CauldronV4 contracts reset the solvency-check flag, letting attackers borrow about 1.79M MIM with no collateral; the DAO bought back the supply to defend the peg.

controls.label: MIM owner Safe
controls.evidence: MIM.owner() returns this Safe. Safe Transaction Service returned threshold 5 with 11 current owners, no modules, and nonce 260; Sourcify ABI for MagicInternetMoneyV1 exposes mint and mintToBentoBox.

review.evidence: Ethereum MIM owner reads and Sourcify ABI identify a 5/11 Safe owner with direct owner-controlled mint functions on the token. Re-verified by direct chain reads at Ethereum block 25575152 on 2026-07-20: MIM 0x99d8a9c45b2eca8864373a26d1459e3dff1e17f3 owner() returns Safe 0x5f0DeE98360d8200b20812e174d139A1a633EDd2, which returns getThreshold()=5 over the same eleven owners, an empty getModulesPaginated array, a zero guard slot, and Safe 1.3.0 masterCopy 0xd9db270c1b5e3bd161e8c8503c55ceabee709552. Economic-control adjudication: the token owner Safe holds unconditional mint and mintToBentoBox entry points with no on-chain cap, no timelock, and no independent bound, so the mint cap is economically unbounded. There is no supply-versus-reserve attestation of any cadence and the token-level owner mint means outstanding MIM cannot be reconciled to cauldron collateral from on-chain reads alone, so reconciliation stays unknown, and no financial regulator supervises Abracadabra. 2026-07-21 follow-up closes the two prior open questions: (1) the verified MagicInternetMoneyV1.sol source shows both mint() and mintToBentoBox() are onlyOwner with no separate cauldron-level minter role — cauldrons draw down MIM the owner has pre-minted into BentoBox rather than minting directly themselves — and mint() itself enforces a soft per-period rate limiter (MINTING_INCREASE=15000/1e5=15% growth of totalSupply per rolling 24-hour MINTING_PERIOD), though the owner can still call mint repeatedly with no absolute ceiling, so the cap remains economically unbounded despite this rate-of-growth throttle; (2) independent owner() reads on Arbitrum (block 486130018) and Avalanche (block 90861407) return 0xf46BB6dDA9709C49EfB918201D97F6474EAc5Aea and 0xae64A325027C3C14Cf6abC7818aA3B9c07F5C799 respectively, matching this asset's separately reviewed bridgeRouteRisk owner() reads for all fourteen deployments (each an Abracadabra team Safe with signer overlap to the Ethereum 5/11 Safe), so the full multichain mint-capable surface is now cross-verified rather than Ethereum-only.
review.reviewer: Codex mint-authority top100 batch-c; Claude V9 Phase 3 curation lane cur-14 (economic-control fields, 2026-07-20); Claude Safety Score V9 curation lane (multichain + rate-limiter resolution, 2026-07-21)
unresolvedQuestions: Establish whether the 5-of-11 owner Safe (or any of the thirteen other chains' team Safes) is subject to any off-chain governance constraint beyond the on-chain Safe threshold; no timelock, guard, or module was detected on any read deployment.

notices.title: Recurring cauldron exploit history
notices.message: Abracadabra/MIM has suffered three material cauldron-related incidents since January 2024: a January 2024 borrow-logic exploit, a March 2025 gmCauldron collateral-accounting exploit, and an October 2025 deprecated CauldronV4 sequencing exploit. Treat cauldron implementation and deprecation risk as recurring protocol risk.

notices.title: Severe depeg and unexplained DAO treasury transfers
notices.message: MIM remained severely depegged as of July 15, 2026. On July 14, Abracadabra-controlled Ethereum and Arbitrum Safes moved roughly $8.3M of treasury assets at then-current prices, including about 2,142 ETH/WETH to a Binance-tagged deposit address and about $4.30M of USDC/USDT to an unlabeled address that immediately forwarded the funds. The Ethereum Safe had also sold 500,000 MIM into Curve on June 8 and 11 for about $489,000. Pharos found no public explanation from Abracadabra as of July 15. These facts do not establish theft, and treasury assets are not MIM's direct cauldron collateral, but the transfers reduce the DAO's transparent onchain treasury backstop while destination control remains unknown.
